label: Relation-of-reason account: cost, decrees under N, joint model
meaning: Clause 1 is proved from the account alone: invariance and the carrier determination give the act at every accessible world; #555's rigid core then excludes strict efficacy; an intrinsic fact in the sense of IntrinsicTo (DEF f8bd9e72, actual-relative supervenience on the source's determinations, admitting necessarily true extrinsic predicates) is constant over the accessible worlds, so it cannot fail at the world lacking the effect; terminus soundness makes the terminus discriminate the effect, and the same world shows it is not intrinsic. So the account keeps contingency and foundation and pays #555's price at the intrinsic level (no strictly sufficient, contrast-relevant intrinsic reason); no intrinsic fact carries the contrast and the terminus, an extrinsic fact, does; on this lane's interpretation (certified by no type) the terminus's variation has no discriminating intrinsic reason, #555's 'relocated' pattern. Clause 2: N at the bearer sends a decree of the family had at an accessible world to w, where exclusivity identifies it with the actual decree; so a real decree excludes a different decree of the family at any alternative (not extra effects under the same decree), the effect's absence needs a world with no decree of the family, and with such a decree at every accessible world the effect is not contingent. Clause 3 is a finite check on one carrier (rr…): the relation-of-reason account with the classical profile premises and a contingent effect. At the root the IX.6 reading with IsImmutable forces ability to be act (Lean-only rootAbilityForced), so that reading is intended; creature potency is restored (the effect is in potency to the impure limiter). The existential PSR holds only through the stipulated reason relation rrExplains, with none of the BX bridges. Nothing in clauses 1-2 mentions intellect, so at the level of the formal account the same price falls on an impersonal permissive propensity whose chance outcome is the terminus; lane P (#2177, causal-perfection-transfer.md, 'The burden is not symmetric') holds that the personal side bears an extra commitment the propensity does not, that its selection is its own free willing and yet not a real determination of it ('That extra commitment falls on the personal side only'); this lane's assessment, not lane P's, is that the commitment is descriptive and that no warrant has been given for counting it as a defect. Structural surrogates only.
